hero.lead: Central Asia’s most populous nation, 37 million strong and growing 7.8% in 2026 on IMF projections, where the World Bank financed $1.1 billion of reforms in 2023 and 2024 and $150 million for rural infrastructure in June 2026.

capital.heading: Reform at speed, financed by its partners.

register.name: Sovereign international bonds in soum (three years, 12.25%)
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · placed 1 April 2026 · UZS 12.2 trillion, about $1bn equivalent · three years · 12.25%, against an indicative 12.5% · orders of UZS 23.4 trillion from nearly 50 foreign investors
register.note: Budget-wide; the largest sovereign international bonds Uzbekistan has placed in its national currency, the Ministry says
register.text: Three-year bonds of the Republic of Uzbekistan in soum, sold to foreign investors at about four times the volume first announced and on average 14 basis points below yields in the domestic market, the Ministry says. The proceeds finance the state budget deficit under the State Budget law for 2026, so they fund the budget as a whole and are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Sovereign international bonds in dollars, euros and soum
register.detail: Ministry of Economy and Finance · orders taken in London on 18 and 20 February 2025 · $500M, seven years, 6.95% · €500M, four years, 5.1%, green · UZS 6 trillion, three years, 15.5% · orders of $4.2bn
register.note: Budget-wide; the euro tranche is a green bond under the SDG financing program
register.text: Three tranches of sovereign international bonds, about $1.5 billion equivalent in all, that finance the state budget deficit for 2025 and resources for commercial banks’ mortgage programs. The Ministry directs the dollar and soum proceeds to housing programs and to building, repairing and rebuilding public schools, preschools and other social infrastructure, and the green euro tranche to projects such as water-saving technologies and waste management, which bear on the shelter, education and water standards.

register.name: Transforming Public Education for Economic Growth Program (BILIM)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 30 June 2026 · $100M of IDA concessional financing and a $5M IFFEd grant · a $378M program, $273M from the government · P513205
register.note: About 2 million children in Grades 1 to 4, half of them girls, and 27,000 new school seats by 2030
register.text: Concessional financing to improve learning in primary schools across six regions, through better teaching and school leadership, new and expanded schools and education data systems, reaching 50,000 teachers, school leaders and administrators. It carries the education standard, the one furthest from reach in Uzbekistan.

register.name: Rural Infrastructure Development Program, second phase
register.detail: World Bank · approved 17 June 2026 · IDA concessional financing · P509427 · six regions
register.note: About 1.2 million rural residents, among them 600,000 women and 300,000 young people
register.text: Concessional financing for public infrastructure and services in rural communities across six regions, including transport, drinking water and electricity, with Common Facility Centers for local entrepreneurs in 15 pilot mahallas. It carries the water, energy and livelihood standards for about 1.2 million rural residents.

register.name: Access to Finance for Jobs and Growth Project (FINGROW)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 15 December 2025 · $100M IBRD loan and a $5M grant · P511700
register.note: About 7,000 small firms expected to gain credit by 2030, 4,500 of them led by women and youth
register.text: Loan guarantees and equity for financially constrained small firms through subsidiaries of the Entrepreneurship Development Company of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, alongside banks, microfinance organisations and private investors. It is expected to lead to 100,000 additional, better-paid jobs, more than half of them for women and young workers, which carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: EduImkon student financing program
register.detail: World Bank · approved 11 December 2025 · IBRD loan · P513279 · implemented by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, 2026 to 2028 · about $30M of private capital expected
register.note: Around 80% of the funds go to loans for low-income students and women
register.text: A loan to strengthen Uzbekistan’s student financing system: wider access to tuition loans, one digital loan platform, closer links between study and the labour market, and a pilot of income-contingent loans. About 600,000 students in higher education and technical and vocational training are expected to be served through 12 commercial banks, which carries the education and livelihood standards.

register.name: First Advancing Global Integration and Market Transition DPO
register.detail: World Bank · approved October 2025, press release of 16 October 2025 · highly concessional loans · first of a programmatic series
register.note: Budget-wide
register.text: Budget support for reforms in nine areas, among them higher compensation payments to low-income households to offset rising electricity, heating and gas tariffs, protection for women at work, social services opened to accredited private and non-governmental providers, agricultural risk insurance and a National Energy Efficiency Agency. It funds the budget as a whole, with measures that bear on the livelihood and energy standards.

register.name: Electricity Distribution Improvement and Strengthening through Commercialization and Transformation
register.detail: World Bank · approved 15 May 2025 · concessional credit · Program-for-Results · P504630 · with $50M from Regional Electric Power Networks, $150M in all
register.note: The World Bank’s first Program-for-Results financing in Uzbekistan
register.text: Financing for Regional Electric Power Networks to modernise and expand distribution over five years: 6,000 km of low-voltage lines, 1,200 transformers and 150,000 smart meters, with the Republic of Karakalpakstan and Surkhandarya among the priority regions. It integrates renewable energy and makes supply more reliable, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Second Inclusive and Resilient Market Economy DPO
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 3 October 2024
register.note: Budget-wide
register.text: Budget support for market reforms.

register.name: Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable People
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 24 May 2024
register.text: Social protection for vulnerable families.

register.name: First Inclusive and Resilient Market Economy DPO
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 7 December 2023
register.note: Budget-wide
register.text: Budget support for market reforms.

register.name: Resilient Livestock Development Project
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · approved 11 November 2026 · concessional loan · project 57079-002 · with $5M of Green Climate Fund grants and $3M from the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific
register.note: About 29,000 smallholder farmers in five major livestock-producing regions
register.text: A concessional loan to strengthen food security and rural livelihoods in Bukhara, Kashkadarya, Navoi, the Republic of Karakalpakstan and Samarkand. It improves access to feed and to drought- and salt-tolerant fodder crops, pasture management and livestock watering points, and veterinary and advisory services with AI-supported pasture monitoring, with training for women livestock farmers, which carries the food and livelihood standards.
by: Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific

register.name: Supplemental Financing to the Green and Resilient Market Economy Climate Policy-Based Financing
register.detail: AIIB · approved 29 October 2026 · sovereign · project 001243 · supplements the program approved on 19 November 2025 · the World Bank co-finances the program
register.note: Budget-wide; listed by AIIB under energy
register.text: Supplemental budget support from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank “to help the Government of Uzbekistan sustain the reform momentum in its ongoing transition to a green economy”. It funds the budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Modernization of Electricity Distribution Systems Program
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · signed 15 October 2026, Bangkok · results-based lending · 60 distribution substations · JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan
register.note: ADB’s first energy operation under its Full Mutual Reliance Framework with the World Bank, which planned a further $100 million
register.text: A loan to upgrade 60 critical distribution substations, add digital network management systems and strengthen the operations of JSC National Electric Grid of Uzbekistan, with training that aims to bring more women into the energy industry. It is expected to lower losses and overloading, make supply more reliable and help enable at least 3.3 gigawatts of renewable capacity, which carries the energy standard for households, businesses and public institutions.

register.name: SmartEd Project
register.detail: Islamic Development Bank · signed 8 February 2026, AlUla · a phase of the IsDB’s total contribution of $160.25M
register.note: A road agreement of $70 million was signed the same day
register.text: The education phase of the financing agreements the Islamic Development Bank and Uzbekistan signed in AlUla. It builds and equips 58 new educational institutions and adds 2,431 classrooms to existing schools, benefiting 72,930 students a year and training more than 36,115 teachers and staff, which carries the education standard.

register.name: Inclusive Finance Sector Development Program, Subprogram 2
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · approved 12 November 2025 · policy-based · $100M of it concessional
register.note: Budget-wide
register.text: Policy-based financing for reforms that widen credit to underserved small businesses, especially those led by women, and modernise microfinance: a higher maximum microloan, revised microfinance and new Islamic microfinance rules, stronger consumer protection and deposit-taking microfinance banks, two of which have preliminary licences. It carries the livelihood standard for the self-employed and microentrepreneurs.

register.name: Project for Promotion of Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings
register.detail: JICA · signed 18 June 2026, Tashkent · ¥21,788M · 2.40%, consulting 0.80% · 25 years with 7 years’ grace · completion October 2032
register.note: A second loan of ¥14,969 million for energy efficiency in industry was signed the same day
register.text: A JICA loan, executed by the National Agency for Energy Efficiency, for energy-efficient equipment and works in schools, preschools and health facilities across Uzbekistan, with consulting services. Lower energy use in public buildings bears on the energy, education and health standards.

register.name: First-loss guarantee for small business loans, Ipak Yuli Bank
register.detail: IFC · 20 July 2026 · Catalytic First Loss Guarantee · $9M first-loss and $9M senior tranches · about $100M equivalent of loans in local currency · expected to mobilise $82M of lending
register.note: The first investment under IFC’s Catalytic First Loss Guarantee Program; the first-loss tranche is counter-guaranteed by the IDA Private Sector Window
register.text: A two-tranche risk-sharing guarantee from IFC behind Ipak Yuli Bank’s loans to microenterprises, climate-related businesses and women-owned enterprises with limited access to finance, with advisory support for the bank. It carries the livelihood standard.

register.name: Mortgage finance, Mortgage Refinancing Company of Uzbekistan
register.detail: EBRD · 18 June 2026 · loan disbursed in synthetic local currency · about €42.7M · medium-term funding
register.note: At least 20% of the funds are expected to support mortgage loans to women
register.text: A loan to the Mortgage Refinancing Company of Uzbekistan, the country’s only mortgage refinancing institution, founded in 2019 with support from state and local banks. It provides medium-term local-currency funding for standardised residential mortgages and affordable housing finance, which carries the shelter standard.

register.name: Bash 2 wind power plant (300 MW), Bukhara
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · signed 6 May 2026, Samarkand · $50M of ADB loans, $41M from commercial lenders arranged by ADB, $25M from LEAP 2 · AIIB and Standard Chartered parallel lenders
register.note: A follow-on to the Bash wind project that ADB cofinanced in 2023
register.text: Financing for a 300-megawatt wind power plant of Acwa in the Bukhara region, with 39 wind turbines of up to 8 megawatts each. It adds renewable power to the grid that serves Uzbekistan’s households and businesses, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Nukus 2 wind and battery storage (200 MW, 100 MWh), Karakalpakstan
register.detail: Asian Development Bank · signed 8 September 2025, Tashkent · $25.4M of ADB ordinary capital and $25.4M from LEAP 2 · a $7.5M ADB credit guarantee backed by the Government of Uzbekistan · AIIB, FMO, Standard Chartered and Saudi EXIM parallel lenders
register.note: Central Asia’s first wind power facility with a utility-scale battery energy storage system, ADB says
register.text: Financing for a 200-megawatt wind power plant with a 100-megawatt-hour battery storage system in the Qoraozak district of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, built by ACWA Power. It is expected to reduce 406,170 tons of CO₂ equivalent emissions a year and brings stored renewable power to the grid, which carries the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 31.3% are under fifteen: the largest young workforce in Central Asia.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Uzbeks working abroad send home a seventh of the economy.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Gold, copper and uranium: mineral rents worth 8.5% of the economy.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Gas that heats the nation and feeds its chemicals industry.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: Imkon Finans
items.text: A microfinance organisation founded in 2011 in Andijan, in the Fergana Valley, that lends for working capital and small investments mainly in rural areas and small towns and was one of the first in the region to offer loans specifically to women entrepreneurs; 53.69% of its loans on Kiva, where it has been an active lending partner since 2024, go to women.

items.name: Fortuna Biznes
items.text: A privately owned microfinance organisation in Fergana, operating since 2018 with eleven branches across six regions, that lends to individual entrepreneurs and small private firms in underserved regions; in 2024 it took the EBRD’s first loan to a microfinance organisation in Uzbekistan, $4 million with up to 35% for businesses led by women.
